items.name: # AGENTS.md
items.annotation: The project description identifies an ML-oriented columnar format emphasizing random access, vector search, versioning and integrations, with an aspirational de facto standard goal. Links delegate additional rules to Rust, Python, Java, protobuf and format-documentation guides. This description is not a benchmark or service guarantee.

items.name: ## File Format Stability and Compatibility
items.annotation: Stable formats require backward and forward compatibility against released stable contracts. Exclusively unstable revisions are disposable and must not accumulate compatibility migrations/tests for prior unstable layouts. Intermediate branch/main states are not released compatibility constraints. Legacy paths no current writer emits are frozen: preserve reading, build new features in current paths, and avoid unrelated legacy refactors. Unavoidable shared-boundary edits must be isolated and covered by released historical fixtures.

items.name: ## Development Commands
items.annotation: Prescribed Rust commands include workspace check with tests/benches; workspace or targeted package tests; clippy --all --tests --benches with warnings denied; cargo fmt --all; nightly llvm-cov branch coverage (optionally HTML); and ci/coverage.py. Use repository profiles, release-with-debug for benchmarks/profiling, and release-no-lto only when appropriate for local debugging, IO-bound or compile-sensitive investigations. These are documented commands, not confirmed successful invocations or proof every named profile is defined in this checkout.

items.name: ## Language-Specific Environment Contract
items.annotation: Language-specific environment instructions must precede tooling. Do not switch managers/toolchains merely because tooling is missing or slow. A command run outside the documented workflow is first an environment usage error; correct usage and rerun before reporting a dependency/tool failure.

items.name: ## Coding Standards
items.annotation: Code/examples/comments use English and prioritize readability; comments explain non-obvious reasons. Remove stdout/debug prints in favor of logging. Add helpers only for real cognitive/duplication benefit, keep PRs focused, avoid collecting RecordBatch streams, and prefer RoaringBitmap to HashSet<u32>. These are maintainer rules, not claims that every existing file complies.

items.name: ### General
items.annotation: Code/examples/comments use English and prioritize readability; comments explain non-obvious reasons. Remove stdout/debug prints in favor of logging. Add helpers only for real cognitive/duplication benefit, keep PRs focused, avoid collecting RecordBatch streams, and prefer RoaringBitmap to HashSet<u32>. These are maintainer rules, not claims that every existing file complies.

items.name: ### Cross-Language Bindings
items.annotation: Keep Python/Java bindings thin and core validation in Rust. Maintain parameter names across languages. Preserve public signatures using deprecation plus new APIs. Replace mutually exclusive booleans with one mode/enum.

items.name: ### Naming
items.annotation: Names describe the value, avoid redundant domain prefixes, consistently use indices, use storage-neutral base terminology, and update every reference when renaming. Validate invalid/mutually exclusive options at boundaries without clamping; errors include relevant names, values, sizes and types.

items.name: ### Error Handling
items.annotation: Names describe the value, avoid redundant domain prefixes, consistently use indices, use storage-neutral base terminology, and update every reference when renaming. Validate invalid/mutually exclusive options at boundaries without clamping; errors include relevant names, values, sizes and types.

items.name: ### Dependencies
items.annotation: Prefer standard/existing dependencies, intentional lock changes, documented pins for broken dependencies and optional feature gates/domain crates. Workspace dependency edits must update root, Python and JNI lockfiles, including cargo check against the excluded Python/JNI manifests; cargo-lock-sync is the stated offline enforcement hook. Actual hook implementation is pending analysis.

items.name: ## Testing Standards
items.annotation: Every feature/bugfix requires tests. Local cases target under one second with small fixtures and split matrices, never weakened assertions/recall. Parameterize input-only differences with named rstest cases or pytest.parametrize; assert rather than print; extend existing tests; skipped tests require issue URLs. Dataset tests include multiple fragments; index cases cover null items/all-null/empty/null columns; vector creation must assert recall >=0.5. Compatibility fixtures live in test_data with datagen.py asserting writer version and copy_test_data_to_tmp for reads.

items.name: ## Documentation Standards
items.annotation: Public APIs need documentation/examples and links; hierarchical diagrams use ASCII; examples follow current signatures; MkDocs admonition bodies use four-space indentation; proofread comments/docs. The KB itself is external documentation, so these describe future repository editing obligations.

items.name: ## Filing Issues
items.annotation: CLI/API-created issues require explicit bug/feature/performance labels because forms are bypassed. Titles use bug:/feature:/perf: with a workflow labeler as fallback, not a replacement for labels.

items.name: ## Pull Requests
items.annotation: Before PR creation search for duplicates and inspect linked PR state/scope. Conventional Commit titles are enforced by commitlint workflow. Before PR creation/update run every touched language's prescribed lint, including full Rust fmt/clippy and Python uv-run lint; if blocked, state the reason in the PR summary. This KB task creates no PR and its no-network/read-only constraints remain in force.

items.name: ## Review Guidelines
items.annotation: Reviews prioritize scarce maintainer attention: concise P0/P1 severe correctness/performance/security findings, avoid repeating praise/change descriptions, and check naming/errors/tests. This review policy does not reduce the user's exhaustive KB scope.

items.name: # Format Documentation Guidelines
items.annotation: The guide inherits root rules. Format doc changes require a PMC vote enforced by format-spec-vote; pair the spec/proto contract and only compilation-required library edits in one PR, implement separately afterward.

items.annotation: The guide inherits root rules. Format doc changes require a PMC vote enforced by format-spec-vote; pair the spec/proto contract and only compilation-required library edits in one PR, implement separately afterward.

items.name: ## Style
items.annotation: Keep format docs concise reference text; place code examples in user guides. Express file schemas as explicit PyArrow schema definitions, and use language-neutral JSON Schema/protobuf rather than Rust structures for general contracts. These rules coexist: schema definitions are expressly required even though illustrative code examples belong elsewhere.

items.name: ## Content
items.annotation: Explain actual evolution mechanics (IDs/tombstones/rewrites), algorithms with parameters, precision, order, normalization and steps, and index file schemas plus navigation/entry-point/page-type distinctions. Naming an algorithm or deferring to an outside spec is insufficient. Bitmap index docs are the referenced pattern, pending their own analysis.

items.name: ## Structure

Group related options in Options/Params objects or builders; use typed enums with explicit Rust serialization rather than Java enum toString spelling and test each enum crossing. Public/IPC handles should be opaque protobuf-backed bytes rather than exposing internal data structures.

items.name: ## Code Style
items.annotation: Prefer imports except ambiguity, JavaBean getXXX accessors for ecosystem compatibility, and Javadoc that repeats relevant Rust defaults/constraints/invariants so callers need no Rust source.

items.name: ## Documentation
items.annotation: Prefer imports except ambiguity, JavaBean getXXX accessors for ecosystem compatibility, and Javadoc that repeats relevant Rust defaults/constraints/invariants so callers need no Rust source.

items.name: Transaction
items.annotation: Transaction exists to rebuild a manifest on retry and determine compatibility after conflict. read_version uint64=1 is the snapshot used for planning/evaluating predicates; uuid string=2 identifies the transaction; tag string=3 is described as optional but lacks scalar presence; transaction_properties string map=4 reserves __lance_commit_message. These fields are not the newly assigned commit version.

items.name: TableIdentifier
items.annotation: TableIdentifier has string uri tag 1, uint64 version tag 2, optional string manifest_etag tag 3, optional bytes serialized_manifest tag 4, and string-to-string storage_options map tag 5. The documented fast mode supplies URI plus serialized manifest so the executor can skip reading a manifest; the lightweight mode supplies URI, version, and ETag so the executor loads it. Presence distinguishes absent optional ETag/manifest from an explicitly present empty value. The schema does not encode mode exclusivity or precedence when both reconstruction forms are supplied; it declares no validation of URI or storage options. Changing tags or presence loses wire meaning.

items.name: IndexType
items.annotation: License, proto3 and lance.index.pb precede Any and index_old.proto imports. IndexType declares only VECTOR=0; this enum is not an exhaustive list of all index kinds in the repository.

items.name: Index
items.annotation: Index has unique dataset index name=1, repeated indexed column names=2, build dataset_version=3, IndexType=4, and implementation oneof VectorIndex vector_index=5. Its shape describes this metadata envelope, not the newer generic Any detail registry.

items.name: Tensor
items.annotation: Tensor.DataType enumerates BFLOAT16=0, FLOAT16=1, FLOAT32=2, FLOAT64=3, UINT8=4, UINT16=5, UINT32=6, UINT64=7. Tensor carries data_type=1, repeated uint32 shape=2, bytes data=3. The comments define shape dimensions but not byte order, strides, validation, or memory alignment.

items.name: IVF
items.annotation: IVF metadata stores repeated float centroids=1 (deprecated in prose, with the actual protobuf deprecated option commented out), repeated uint64 partition offsets=2, repeated uint32 record lengths=3, Tensor centroids_tensor=4, and optional double KMeans loss=5. Centroid shape is num_partitions by dimension. Implementations must decide compatibility precedence; this schema does not say what happens if both centroid forms are populated.

items.name: PQ
items.annotation: PQ records num_bits=1, num_sub_vectors=2, dimension=3, repeated float codebook=4, and Tensor codebook_tensor=5. Both codebook descriptions require dimension times 2^num_bits scalar values. This is metadata, not the sub-vector layout or distance implementation; no legal-bit-range validation appears.

items.name: TransformType
items.annotation: TransformType declares OPQ=0. Transform stores matrix file position=1, repeated uint32 shape [rows,cols]=2, and transform type=3. Flat is an empty marker. These encode stage descriptions without executing a transformation.

items.name: Transform
items.annotation: TransformType declares OPQ=0. Transform stores matrix file position=1, repeated uint32 shape [rows,cols]=2, and transform type=3. Flat is an empty marker. These encode stage descriptions without executing a transformation.

items.name: Flat
items.annotation: TransformType declares OPQ=0. Transform stores matrix file position=1, repeated uint32 shape [rows,cols]=2, and transform type=3. Flat is an empty marker. These encode stage descriptions without executing a transformation.

items.name: DiskAnn
items.annotation: DiskAnn carries spec=1, filename=2, r=3, alpha=4, capital-L field L=5, and repeated graph entry IDs=6. The schema supplies parameter names but not the graph algorithm or numeric bounds. VectorIndexStage.stage selects Flat=1, IVF=2, PQ=3, Transform=4, or DiskAnn=5; retaining order in the surrounding repeated stage list is essential to represent a pipeline. Ordered pipeline example: protos/index.proto:176-184.

items.name: VectorIndexStage
items.annotation: DiskAnn carries spec=1, filename=2, r=3, alpha=4, capital-L field L=5, and repeated graph entry IDs=6. The schema supplies parameter names but not the graph algorithm or numeric bounds. VectorIndexStage.stage selects Flat=1, IVF=2, PQ=3, Transform=4, or DiskAnn=5; retaining order in the surrounding repeated stage list is essential to represent a pipeline. Ordered pipeline example: protos/index.proto:176-184.

items.name: VectorMetricType
items.annotation: VectorMetricType declares L2=0, Cosine=1, Dot=2, Hamming=3. VectorIndex stores spec_version=1, dimension=2, repeated stages=3, metric_type=4; its example composes IVF then PQ with 8 bits and 16 subvectors. The enum names do not specify normalization or squared-versus-unsquared numeric outputs.

items.name: VectorIndex
items.annotation: VectorMetricType declares L2=0, Cosine=1, Dot=2, Hamming=3. VectorIndex stores spec_version=1, dimension=2, repeated stages=3, metric_type=4; its example composes IVF then PQ with 8 bits and 16 subvectors. The enum names do not specify normalization or squared-versus-unsquared numeric outputs.

items.name: VectorIndexDetails
items.annotation: VectorIndexDetails is stored in manifest index_details. metric_type=1 chooses metric; target_partition_size=2 uses zero for unset; optional HnswParameters=3 indicates an HNSW layer. Nested ProductQuantization has num_bits=1 and num_sub_vectors=2; ScalarQuantization has num_bits=1; RabitQuantization has num_bits=1 and RotationType=2 with FAST=0, MATRIX=1; FlatCompression is empty and means stored unquantized vectors.

items.name: HnswParameters
items.annotation: HnswParameters has max_connections=1 (M, outgoing-edge bound: more improves recall at memory/build cost), construction_ef=2 (dynamic candidate list size during construction), and max_level=3. Defaults, legality checks, and exact complexity are not given.

items.name: JsonIndexDetails
items.annotation: JsonIndexDetails stores JSON path string=1 and google.protobuf.Any target_details=2, allowing nested index-kind details. BloomFilterIndexDetails, RTreeIndexDetails, and FMIndexDetails are empty markers. Empty metadata messages do not imply empty index files or lack of implementation options.

items.name: BloomFilterIndexDetails
items.annotation: JsonIndexDetails stores JSON path string=1 and google.protobuf.Any target_details=2, allowing nested index-kind details. BloomFilterIndexDetails, RTreeIndexDetails, and FMIndexDetails are empty markers. Empty metadata messages do not imply empty index files or lack of implementation options.

items.name: RTreeIndexDetails
items.annotation: JsonIndexDetails stores JSON path string=1 and google.protobuf.Any target_details=2, allowing nested index-kind details. BloomFilterIndexDetails, RTreeIndexDetails, and FMIndexDetails are empty markers. Empty metadata messages do not imply empty index files or lack of implementation options.

items.name: FMIndexDetails
items.annotation: JsonIndexDetails stores JSON path string=1 and google.protobuf.Any target_details=2, allowing nested index-kind details. BloomFilterIndexDetails, RTreeIndexDetails, and FMIndexDetails are empty markers. Empty metadata messages do not imply empty index files or lack of implementation options.

items.name: MinHashLshIndexDetails
items.annotation: MinHashLshIndexDetails is explicitly experimental: incompatible detail/file changes may require rebuilding the index, not rewriting data, and the feature may be removed if stabilization fails. Every segment must share identical details, query signatures must be comparable, and both index files repeat serialized details in schema metadata to detect mismatches. Readers validate every field before allocation or file read. num_hashes=1 is in [1,4096] and divisible by num_bands; num_bands=2 is in [1,256]; each band covers num_hashes/num_bands consecutive values.

items.name: FileDescriptor
items.annotation: License, proto3, and lance.file package precede FileDescriptor(schema=1,length uint64=2). Schema describes contents and length counts file rows. This message does not embed actual column buffers.

items.name: Schema
items.annotation: Schema has repeated lance.file.Field fields=1 including nested fields, and string-to-bytes metadata map=5. Its field list is not limited to top-level columns and its metadata values need not be UTF-8 strings.

items.name: Metadata
items.annotation: Metadata reserves tag 4 because StatisticsMetadata previously used it and older readers had a bug. manifest_position uint64=1 uses zero to indicate externally stored manifest. batch_offsets repeated int32=2 is described as logical offsets of chunk groups, with a parenthetical about rows in each chunk; exact offset-versus-count conversion is an implementation question rather than a reason to reinterpret the declaration.

items.name: Encoding
items.annotation: Encoding enum assigns NONE=0 invalid, PLAIN=1, VAR_BINARY=2, DICTIONARY=3, RLE=4. Dictionary stores signed int64 offset=1 and length=2 for dictionary values; offset is meaningful only with DICTIONARY and logical_type describes the values' type. These declarations do not prove all enum alternatives have active implementations.

items.name: Dictionary
items.annotation: Encoding enum assigns NONE=0 invalid, PLAIN=1, VAR_BINARY=2, DICTIONARY=3, RLE=4. Dictionary stores signed int64 offset=1 and length=2 for dictionary values; offset is meaningful only with DICTIONARY and logical_type describes the values' type. These declarations do not prove all enum alternatives have active implementations.

items.name: Field
items.annotation: Field.Type distinguishes PARENT=0, REPEATED=1, LEAF=2. Fields are Type type=1, fully qualified name string=2, signed id=3, and signed parent_id=4. ID assignment refers to DataFile.fields. The parent comment says not-set means top-level, but parent_id is a bare proto3 int32 without presence; the actual sentinel/default convention must come from conversion code. Do not assume Option semantics.

items.name: U64Range
items.annotation: License, proto3, lance.datafusion, and table_identifier.proto import establish the envelope. U64Range has uint64 start=1 and end=2. This file does not state whether its endpoint is exclusive; that must be checked in conversions rather than inferred from the field names.

items.name: ProjectionProto
items.annotation: ProjectionProto carries repeated int32 field_ids=1 and independent bool flags with_row_id=2, with_row_addr=3, with_row_last_updated_at_version=4, with_row_created_at_version=5, plus BlobHandlingProto blob_handling=6. Row identity, address, and version metadata are separate projection choices, not one combined switch.

items.name: BlobHandlingProto
items.annotation: BlobHandlingProto.mode is a oneof: all_binary=1 reads all blobs as binary; blobs_descriptions=2 uses descriptions for blobs and binary for other binary columns (commented default); all_descriptions=3 describes all binary columns; some_blobs_binary=4 materializes specified blobs while non-blob binary remains binary; some_binary=5 materializes selected binary columns and describes the rest. The first three variants are bool-tagged arms; the latter two use FieldIdSet with repeated uint32 field_ids=1. Selecting a oneof arm is semantically distinct from the boolean payload; actual rejection/handling of false markers is not specified.

items.name: FieldIdSet
items.annotation: BlobHandlingProto.mode is a oneof: all_binary=1 reads all blobs as binary; blobs_descriptions=2 uses descriptions for blobs and binary for other binary columns (commented default); all_descriptions=3 describes all binary columns; some_blobs_binary=4 materializes specified blobs while non-blob binary remains binary; some_binary=5 materializes selected binary columns and describes the rest. The first three variants are bool-tagged arms; the latter two use FieldIdSet with repeated uint32 field_ids=1. Selecting a oneof arm is semantically distinct from the boolean payload; actual rejection/handling of false markers is not specified.

items.name: FilteredReadThreadingModeProto
items.annotation: FilteredReadThreadingModeProto.mode selects uint64 one_partition_multiple_threads=1 or multiple_partitions=2. The wire shape keeps these choices mutually exclusive. The precise interpretation and validation of their counts require the Rust threading-mode conversion.

items.name: FilteredReadOptionsProto
items.annotation: FilteredReadOptionsProto has optional before/after filter ranges tags 1/2, with_deleted_rows=3, optional batch_size=4, optional fragment_readahead=5, repeated fragment_ids=6, projection=7, optional refine_filter_substrait=8 and full_filter_substrait=9 bytes, threading_mode=10, optional io_buffer_size_bytes=11, and optional filter_schema_ipc=12. The IPC filter schema may be wider than the output projection so omitted output columns can still participate in filter decoding. Defaults and semantics of an empty fragment list are not supplied by these declarations.

items.name: FilteredReadPlanProto
items.annotation: FilteredReadPlanProto serializes RowAddrTreeMap through its own serialize_into/deserialize_from into bytes tag 1; optional after-filter range is tag 2 and matching encode-time filter IPC schema tag 3. fragment_filter_ids tag 4 maps uint32 fragment IDs to uint32 indices into repeated Substrait filter_expressions tag 5, deduplicating shared predicates. These values are list positions, not external predicate IDs; index validity must be checked by implementation.

items.name: FilteredReadExecProto
items.annotation: FilteredReadExecProto stores TableIdentifier table=1, options=2, and optional plan=3. The documented distributed mode receives a planned FilteredReadPlan; local mode plans at execution. index_input is intentionally absent here: DataFusion PhysicalExtensionCodec traverses child plans using children()/with_new_children() and supplies decoded inputs to try_decode. Every child needs compatible codec handling. The TODO to implement Lance index-input codecs is a comment about intended work, not proof that the current implementation still lacks every codec.

items.name: RowIdSequence
items.annotation: RowIdSequence.segments tag 1 is an ordered repeated U64Segment sequence. Segment encodings favor sorted and differently sparse IDs. Nested U64Segment.Range uses uint64 start=1 inclusive and end=2 exclusive; empty or reversed-range validation is not encoded here.

items.name: U64Segment
items.annotation: RowIdSequence.segments tag 1 is an ordered repeated U64Segment sequence. Segment encodings favor sorted and differently sparse IDs. Nested U64Segment.Range uses uint64 start=1 inclusive and end=2 exclusive; empty or reversed-range validation is not encoded here.

items.name: EncodedU64Array
items.annotation: EncodedU64Array contains U16Array(base uint64=1, offsets bytes=2), U32Array(base uint64=1, offsets bytes=2), and U64Array(values bytes=2). Offsets are unsigned 16- or 32-bit deltas; bytes avoid unsupported uint16 and uint32 varint overhead, while full u64 bytes avoid varints. The array oneof selects u16_array=1, u32_array=2, or u64_array=3. Endianness, alignment, and overflow checks are not stated, so exact byte decoding requires the Rust implementation. The heading calls this bitpacked, whereas declarations explicitly provide fixed-width byte variants; retain that distinction.

items.name: RowDatasetVersionSequence
items.annotation: RowDatasetVersionSequence stores repeated RowDatasetVersionRun runs=1 for runs of equal dataset versions. Each run carries U64Segment span=1 and uint64 version=2. The span comment describes the number of consecutive rows, but its declared type is a segment rather than a scalar count; do not replace it with a count or assume how it is interpreted without checking the converter.

items.name: RowDatasetVersionRun
items.annotation: RowDatasetVersionSequence stores repeated RowDatasetVersionRun runs=1 for runs of equal dataset versions. Each run carries U64Segment span=1 and uint64 version=2. The span comment describes the number of consecutive rows, but its declared type is a segment rather than a scalar count; do not replace it with a count or assume how it is interpreted without checking the converter.

items.name: UUID
items.annotation: The opening historical-looking layout diagram lists encoded chunks, indices, chunk-position matrix, optional manifest, metadata, i64 metadata position, version pair and LANC. It is not the newer file2 footer diagram and should not be applied to every current file. UUID is a message with bytes uuid=1 documented as exactly 16 bytes; no validation is implemented in protobuf.

items.name: Manifest
items.annotation: Manifest carries repeated lance.file.Field fields=1 including nested fields, repeated DataFragment fragments=2, uint64 version=3, uint64 version_aux_data=4, and bytes-valued schema_metadata map=5. fragment_tree=22 replaces the inline fragment list for tree tables: fragments must be empty and bit 12 set in both feature words so unaware readers do not see an empty dataset. Auxiliary data is version-specific, not inherited, and not loaded by default on query.

items.name: BasePath
items.annotation: base_paths repeated BasePath=18 resolves imported, shallow-cloned or multi-tier files; example resolves ID zero as base/data/file.path and IDs increase from zero. branch optional string=20 uses absence for main. BasePath has id uint32=1, optional alias name=2 (source tag for shallow clone), is_dataset_root bool=3 distinguishing dataset roots with data/_deletions subdirectories from direct file directories, and absolute path string=4 parsed directly. The comment refers to lance.file.File/DeletionFile, but actual declarations are lance.table.DataFile/DeletionFile (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:6-6; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:90-90; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:257-257).

items.name: VersionAuxData
items.annotation: VersionAuxData is loaded on demand and has metadata map<string,bytes>=3. Its absence/default loading policy comes from Manifest.version_aux_data; it is not table configuration.

items.name: IndexMetadata
items.annotation: IndexMetadata.uuid message=1 is unique across dataset versions; fields repeated int32=2 refers to logical Field IDs and preserves key order; name string=3 is unique within a version; dataset_version uint64=4 is the build version. With manifest bit 13 fields contains keys only; otherwise legacy carried values form the trailing suffix. The same bytes have different interpretation depending on the manifest flag, making atomic migration mandatory.

items.name: IndexFile
items.annotation: IndexFile has index-directory-relative path string=1 and size_bytes uint64=2. IndexSection contains repeated IndexMetadata indices=1 for one dataset version. A comment records VectorIndexDetails and renamed HnswParameters moving to index.proto; it is not another declaration.

items.name: IndexSection
items.annotation: IndexFile has index-directory-relative path string=1 and size_bytes uint64=2. IndexSection contains repeated IndexMetadata indices=1 for one dataset version. A comment records VectorIndexDetails and renamed HnswParameters moving to index.proto; it is not another declaration.

items.name: FragmentReuseIndexDetails
items.annotation: FragmentReuseIndexDetails.content chooses InlineContent inline=1 or ExternalFile external=2; comment threshold is below 200 KB inline, otherwise external InlineContent bytes, with exact unit/threshold selection to verify in code. InlineContent stores historical Version legacy_versions=1 and new Transition transitions=2 requiring index_version=1. Transition has source FragmentDigests=1 in scan order including deleted rows, destinations=2 in label order with creation counts, and exactly one ordered_compaction=3 or stable_partition=4 mapping. New safe backward-compatible mappings, including scan fallback, need no version bump; unsafe ones do. Ordered compaction concatenates surviving source rows in scan order then splits; stable partition distributes sequential source rows by destination label.

items.name: ShardStatus
items.annotation: The MemWAL section introduces ShardStatus ACTIVE=0 and SEALED=1. Drop-table two-phase commit seals a shard to refuse claims reversibly, then deletes on commit or returns ACTIVE on rollback. ShardManifest documents exactly one active writer per shard; shard_id UUID=11 is v4, version uint64=1 matches manifest filename, shard_spec_id uint32=10 is immutable at creation with zero for manual/unmanaged shards, and shard_field_entries repeated=14 stores raw Arrow scalar bytes keyed by field ID and interpreted by ShardingSpec.result_type. The comment explicitly gives little-endian int32 and raw UTF-8 examples.

items.name: ShardManifest
items.annotation: The MemWAL section introduces ShardStatus ACTIVE=0 and SEALED=1. Drop-table two-phase commit seals a shard to refuse claims reversibly, then deletes on commit or returns ACTIVE on rollback. ShardManifest documents exactly one active writer per shard; shard_id UUID=11 is v4, version uint64=1 matches manifest filename, shard_spec_id uint32=10 is immutable at creation with zero for manual/unmanaged shards, and shard_field_entries repeated=14 stores raw Arrow scalar bytes keyed by field ID and interpreted by ShardingSpec.result_type. The comment explicitly gives little-endian int32 and raw UTF-8 examples.

items.name: ShardFieldEntry
items.annotation: ShardFieldEntry has field_id string=1 matching ShardingField.field_id and value bytes=2 in raw little-endian Arrow representation; matching result_type gives the data type. There is no self-describing per-value type tag here.

items.name: SsTable
items.annotation: SsTable is an immutable flushed MemTable stored as a Lance dataset. generation uint64=1 and shard-relative path string=2 identify it. Optional in_memory_bytes=3 estimates accounted buffer windows, excluding reader array structure and requiring headroom; absent means unknown, not zero. Optional physical_rows=4 includes older primary-key duplicates masked by its deletion vector. Optional primary_key_bytes=5 sums key-column payload over all physical rows, is not per-row/encoded-sort-key size, and is also absent without a primary key. Treating these estimates as hard bounds or defaults as zero risks underbudgeting.

items.name: CompactedSsTable
items.annotation: CompactedSsTable has shard_id UUID=1 and generation uint64=2 for latest compaction into base data. IndexCatchupProgress has base index_name=1 (must match maintained_indexes) and caught_up_generations repeated=2. The protobuf comment says an absent shard means unknown progress, requiring retained SSTables and repair. This conflicts with the Rust getter comment saying absence is assumed fully caught up; the getter itself simply returns None (rust/lance-table/src/system_index/mem_wal.rs:157-164). Complete consumers must resolve policy; neither comment proves safe deletion.

items.name: IndexCatchupProgress
items.annotation: CompactedSsTable has shard_id UUID=1 and generation uint64=2 for latest compaction into base data. IndexCatchupProgress has base index_name=1 (must match maintained_indexes) and caught_up_generations repeated=2. The protobuf comment says an absent shard means unknown progress, requiring retained SSTables and repair. This conflicts with the Rust getter comment saying absence is assumed fully caught up; the getter itself simply returns None (rust/lance-table/src/system_index/mem_wal.rs:157-164). Complete consumers must resolve policy; neither comment proves safe deletion.

items.name: MemWalIndexDetails

items.annotation: The guide inherits root cross-language standards and introduces Rust code style.

items.name: ## Concurrency
items.annotation: spawn_cpu closures must compute and return without channel waits, IO, locks, block_on or blocking APIs. The guide warns that resource-constrained pools can have one worker and deadlock when blocked; keep waiting outside in async code and dispatch substantial (~100 microseconds+) CPU work. This is policy and a rule of thumb, not a measured threshold. Actual sizing includes an explicit thread override and configurable IO reservation, so the guide's <=3-CPU example is not universal under all settings. Implementation: rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:23-76; rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:135-208.

items.name: ## API Design
items.annotation: Builder option methods use with_, APIs prefer Into/AsRef, internals prefer pub(crate), public re-exports define the surface, and enums/typed structs replace magic numbers/unstructured maps. Keep physical RowAddr and stable RowId distinct; use RowAddress helpers and Roaring/RowAddrTreeMap selections. User counts subtract deletions; traits stay minimal; schema introspection must not materialize rows. Persistent formats are stable/versioned; Arrow access uses typed accessors (optional variants unless type proven); local IO writes use single syscalls instead of cloud multipart machinery.

items.name: ## Error Handling
items.annotation: Fallible library paths return contextual Result errors rather than panics/unwraps; use NotSupported instead of TODO/unimplemented, classify errors by cause, checked arithmetic for IDs/counters, debug assertions for non-safety invariants, and explicit handling of impossible states. A subsequent narrower rule permits expect with a reason only when unavoidable; this is not encouragement to bypass the earlier fallible-path prohibition. Warn for cleanup failures/silent no-ops, avoid duplicate warning-before-error, reject missing required config rather than defaulting, and advance/bind parallel iterators exactly once before skipping work.

items.name: ## Naming
items.annotation: Only truly unused bindings use underscore prefixes; booleans use is_/has_ and choose a desired zero/default state (disable_* for default-enabled behavior). Names describe actual scope rather than a broader operation.

items.name: ## Testing
items.annotation: Tests use record_batch! or gen_batch setup, try_into_batch for scans, plain memory:// storage, and assertions on both error variant and text. These rules specify meaningful tests without asserting any current suite passes.

items.name: ## Documentation
items.annotation: Public docs explain semantic constraints/effects, enum variants, magic constants and fallback conditions. Describe mutation versus returned values correctly, mark future work TODO/FIXME, explain both Option states and use precise domain terms.

items.name: ## lance-encoding
items.annotation: Encoding hot paths hoist invariant branches, preallocate contiguous zero-initialized buffers by default, restrict unsafe set_len to measured hot paths with a SAFETY justification that all bytes are initialized before reading, dispatch spawn_cpu only at the async/CPU boundary without nesting, and use existing next-item helpers. The rule does not prove any specific unsafe block is sound.

items.name: pub trait DeepSizeOf {
items.annotation: DeepSizeOf is public. Its default deep_size_of adds size_of_val(self) to deep_size_of_children with a fresh Context; the latter is required and receives mutable traversal state. Implementations must count descendant heap storage without recounting their own inline footprint and should propagate the same context when deduplication is intended.

items.annotation: parse_nested_rep consumes little-endian u64 words using stride words per chunk. num_chunks floors (bytes.len()/8)/stride; zero stride divides by zero, stride one can overlap words then overrun, and trailing bytes/incomplete groups are not locally rejected. items.name: pub struct FileReader {
items.annotation: Public FileReader derives Clone and DeepSizeOf. object_reader is a public Arc<dyn Reader>; metadata and ordinary page table are private Arcs, schema is owned, fragment_id is private u64, and statistics is an Arc<Option<PageTable>>. Cloning shares reader/tables/metadata and clones Schema according to its own Clone semantics, including shared dictionary arrays. Public replacement of object_reader does not refresh any stored metadata/schema/table. There is no custom Drop.

items.name: impl std::fmt::Debug for FileReader {
items.annotation: Debug prints only fragment ID and object_reader.path; it does not dump schema, metadata, dictionaries or page tables. fragment_id is otherwise only set and retained in this file: no row-ID column or bitwise address construction occurs here despite later constructor documentation.

items.name: impl FileReader {
items.annotation: Public traced try_new_with_fragment_id opens the ObjectStore path, loads metadata, then forwards the supplied Schema, u32 fragment ID, signed min/max field bounds and optional LanceCache to try_new_from_reader with Some(metadata). No schema/dictionary hydration is performed here. Docs mention an optional manifest and row-ID high bits, but the actual signature requires Schema and this file emits no row IDs. IO/cache errors propagate before reader construction.

items.name: pub fn batches_stream(
items.annotation: Public batches_stream consumes FileReader, Schema and a mutable Send+Sync static batch-ID predicate. It snapshots num_batches as i32, lazily filters IDs in increasing order, retains reader/projection in Arcs and reads whole batches with fixed buffered(2), independent of Reader io_parallelism for this outer layer. The stream adapter advertises the supplied projection schema; each batch may still perform parallel field reads. No Tokio task is spawned here despite thread-sharing comments; dropping the stream drops pending local futures, without a backend cancellation guarantee.

items.name: pub async fn read_batch(
items.annotation: Public free read_batch rejects an empty schema with InvalidInput no fields requested. Its comment about with_row_id and panic is stale: no such flag or row-ID synthesis exists. Nonempty roots are read concurrently via ordered buffered(reader parallelism), collected, then RecordBatch::try_new checks assembled arrays against converted explicit schema. No upfront batch-ID validation occurs; missing page errors or codec errors emerge during reads.

items.name: async fn read_array(
items.annotation: Private async-recursive read_array reconstructs field.data_type and first routes is_fixed_stride to plain decoding. Otherwise handles Null, four binary/string families, Struct, Dictionary, List<Int32 offsets> and LargeList<Int64 offsets>. Other types panic via unimplemented rather than returning NotSupported. In the locally read predicate every FSL is fixed-stride, regardless of child; Interval has byte_width support but is absent from is_fixed_stride, so predicate/type-dispatch differences matter (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:111-181). No field.encoding tag drives this dispatch.

items.name: fn get_page_info<'a>(
items.annotation: get_page_info looks up exact signed field.id and batch_id in the provided PageTable. Missing entry becomes InvalidInput with field name, field ID and batch ID. It performs no file-bound or length validation on the returned PageInfo.

items.name: async fn _read_fixed_stride_array(
items.annotation: _read_fixed_stride_array fetches page info from its supplied table, reconstructs field DataType and forwards position, length and cloned selector to the V1 facade. It passes neither field.nullable nor a separate validity bitmap; plain codec semantics govern primitive/fixed-array null handling.

items.name: fn read_null_array(
items.annotation: read_null_array obtains page info but performs no payload IO. Empty Indices produces0; nonempty raw indices.values determines maximum, rejecting max>=page length, then uses indices.len. Index validity is ignored, so null selector backing values participate in bounds checks and every selector slot counts as a Null output row.

items.name: async fn read_binary_array(
items.annotation: Binary adapter gets page info and forwards actual field DataType, field.nullable, position/length and borrowed selector to the V1 binary facade. Nullable controls equal-offset-to-null reconstruction; no independent validity is fetched here. Missing-page errors precede binary selector validation.

items.name: async fn read_dictionary_array(
items.annotation: Dictionary adapter gets page info, reconstructs DataType and unwraps field.dictionary plus its loaded values before constructing DictionaryDecoder. It clones the values Arc, then forwards cloned selector. Missing/unhydrated dictionaries panic, even for a selector whose key decoder might otherwise return empty; this layer does not hydrate or validate dictionary values.

items.name: async fn read_struct_array(
items.annotation: Struct adapter walks field.children sequentially, recursively reading each with the same table/batch/selector, then creates StructArray from FieldRef/ArrayRef pairs. It never reads a page or validity bitmap for the struct parent, so original parent nullness is not reconstructed. Child failures short-circuit after any earlier IO; there is no parallel child scheduling or parent-level row-count validation here.

items.name: async fn take_list_array<T: ArrowNumericType>(
items.annotation: Generic take_list_array expects a nonempty sorted UInt32 selector. It subtracts the first selector from every raw selector value and indexes the already fetched position span to create per-list child ranges. Null selector validity is ignored, and unsigned subtraction, positions and first-child existence are unchecked. It clones the Field and accumulates arrays rather than streaming child values.

items.name: async fn read_list_array<T: ArrowNumericType>(
items.annotation: read_list_array expands Range end and RangeTo end by1 for the terminal offset; Indices reads the entire first..last+2 position interval. RangeFull/from pass through unchanged. Empty direct Indices panics at first/last access before page lookup; no sorting or validity checks are local. Arithmetic is unchecked. Multiple Ranges is initially passed through to fixed-stride decoding.

A row represents all arrays supplied to one collection, not necessarily one Arrow batch. Bound absence is represented in typed ScalarValue options and differs by algorithm.

items.name: fn compute_primitive_statistics<T: ArrowNumericType>(
items.annotation: compute_primitive_statistics<T:ArrowNumericType> requires Native:Bounded+PartialOrd, starts min at native maximum and max at native minimum, casts every array to T, sums physical null counts as i64, skips arrays whose entire length is null (including empty arrays), then compares only Some values. all_values_null becomes false upon any non-all-null array. If no valid value exists, return full native [MIN,MAX] and accumulated null count, not null bounds. No checked null-count conversion/sum, mixed-type validation or data concatenation occurs.

items.name: fn get_statistics<T: ArrowNumericType>(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow
items.annotation: get_statistics<T> debug-asserts nonempty outer input, calls primitive reduction, and constructs nonnull primitive ScalarValues using arrays[0].data_type(), unwrapping both conversions. Using the actual first DataType preserves temporal parameters such as timezone rather than generic T::DATA_TYPE. Later arrays are downcast but no cross-array parameter equality check occurs locally. Empty outer input can panic at first-array indexing even without debug assertions.

items.name: fn compute_float_statistics<T: ArrowNumericType>(
items.annotation: compute_float_statistics<T> initializes [+infinity,-infinity], sums physical null counts before skipping all-null/empty arrays, and changes bounds only for strict partial_cmp Greater/Less. NaN comparisons produce no update, but NaNs do not increment null_count. If both sentinels remain unchanged, replace them with [-infinity,+infinity], covering empty, all-null and all-NaN input. Actual single positive or negative infinity updates the opposite bound, preserving a constant-infinity interval.

items.name: fn get_float_statistics<T: ArrowNumericType>(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow
items.annotation: get_float_statistics uses the float reducer, normalizes any minimum equal to zero to negative zero and any maximum equal to negative zero to positive zero; floating equality covers both zero signs. Converts the resulting native numbers through ScalarValue::from; returns nonnull bounds even for no ordered value. No total-order NaN comparison or timezone/type parameter is involved for Float32/64.

items.name: fn get_decimal_statistics(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
items.annotation: get_decimal_statistics reuses Decimal128 native i128 reduction, then reads precision and scale from the first array and wraps both values without precision validation here. No Decimal256 branch exists. Empty/all-null Decimal128 therefore uses native i128 extrema rather than decimal-precision-limited extrema; downstream scalar/Arrow conversion may impose separate constraints, not checked by this reducer.

items.name: fn truncate_utf8(data: &str, length: usize) -> Option<&str> {
items.annotation: truncate_utf8 asserts data.len()>=length, walks char_indices backward over the original entire string, and returns the longest NONEMPTY valid prefix whose ending byte offset is <=length. It returns None when no full character fits, including length0; it never manufactures Some(empty). The comment says less than length, but actual condition permits equality. Backward traversal may scan the long suffix; the 64-byte comparison limit does not make truncation constant-time in input length. Caller invokes it only for strings longer than64, where at least one Unicode scalar fits.

items.name: fn increment_utf8(mut data: Vec<u8>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
items.annotation: increment_utf8 owns bytes and tries indices right-to-left. For each index it repeatedly increments that byte up to overflow, validating the entire candidate with str::from_utf8 after each attempt; first valid candidate is returned. On exhausting a byte it restores its original value before trying the previous position. Unlike binary carry it does not zero the suffix, change byte length, or construct the next Unicode scalar across multiple changed bytes. A lexically greater same-length valid candidate is conservative; None means this algorithm found none, not a proof that no Unicode upper bound of another form exists. Empty input also returns None.

items.name: fn truncate_binary(data: &[u8], length: usize) -> Option<&[u8]> {
items.annotation: truncate_binary asserts input length>=requested length and always returns Some(exact prefix of that length), including zero; there is no all-maximal-byte special case despite the adjacent comment. increment performs big-endian-style carry from the last byte: overflow writes0 and continues left, first nonoverflow returns the same-length vector. All0xFF or empty input returns None. Both less-than comments are imprecise: a prefix may equal the stated length.

items.name: fn increment(mut data: Vec<u8>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
items.annotation: truncate_binary asserts input length>=requested length and always returns Some(exact prefix of that length), including zero; there is no all-maximal-byte special case despite the adjacent comment. increment performs big-endian-style carry from the last byte: overflow writes0 and continues left, first nonoverflow returns the same-length vector. All0xFF or empty input returns None. Both less-than comments are imprecise: a prefix may equal the stated length.

items.name: fn get_string_statistics<T: OffsetSizeTrait>(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
items.annotation: get_string_statistics<T:OffsetSizeTrait> casts each array to the chosen UTF8 offset width, accumulates null counts and skips all-null/empty arrays. Each nonnull string longer than64 bytes is truncated at a UTF8 boundary and sets one global bounds_truncated flag. Min/max compare these prefixes lexically with strict comparisons, keeping borrowed references until final ownership conversion. Any truncated value sets the flag even if it never supplies the maximum; short values and empty strings remain eligible.

items.name: fn get_binary_statistics<T: OffsetSizeTrait>(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
items.annotation: get_binary_statistics<T> mirrors string reduction using generic binary casts and raw byte lexicographic ordering. It truncates each value longer than64 to exactly64 bytes, sets a global truncation flag, and compares borrowed slices. Accumulates null counts for every array before skipping all-null/empty arrays. Input consistency is assumed rather than validated.

items.name: fn get_fixed_size_binary_statistics(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
items.annotation: get_fixed_size_binary_statistics obtains declared width from the first array, sets do_truncate if width>64, then scans nonnull values with lexical byte comparison, truncating each to64 if enabled. Accumulates physical null counts, skips all-null arrays, and assumes common width/type across arrays. Width<=64 compares full values. This helper is callable by the dispatcher but excluded from automatic collector eligibility.

items.name: fn get_boolean_statistics(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
items.annotation: get_boolean_statistics tracks presence of true/false and sums each array null count before an early continue. Once both values have appeared, later arrays need not be scanned for values but still contribute nulls. Within the current array the for_each does not break early. Bounds are Some(true_present&&!false_present) and Some(true_present||!false_present): onlytrue gives true/true, onlyfalse false/false, mixed false/true, no valid values false/true.

items.name: fn cast_dictionary_arrays<'a, T: ArrowDictionaryKeyType + 'static>(
items.annotation: cast_dictionary_arrays<T> downcasts every dictionary and collects borrowed Arc references to each complete VALUES array into a new Vec. It does not follow keys, deduplicate shared dictionaries, slice values to referenced entries or include key null counts. The returned lifetime is tied to input references.

items.name: fn get_dictionary_statistics(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
items.annotation: get_dictionary_statistics inspects the first Dictionary key type and dispatches Int8/16/32/64 or UInt8/16/32/64 to value extraction, then recursively collect_statistics on those full values arrays. Returned bound scalar type is the dictionary VALUE type. Null count is the sum of values-array null counts, possibly repeatedly counting the same shared dictionary; it is not decoded-row/key null count. Unused dictionary entries affect bounds. Unsupported key type panics naming key type, non-Dictionary call panics naming actual type. This helper remains outside automatic collector selection.

items.name: fn get_temporal_statistics(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
items.annotation: get_temporal_statistics maps Time32 Second/Millisecond, Time64 Microsecond/Nanosecond, Date32/64, all four Timestamp units and all four Duration units to corresponding primitive marker. Timestamp timezone propagates via get_statistics first-array DataType; values are not timezone converted. Other unit/type combinations are unreachable. Native integer extrema supply empty/all-null bounds; temporal domain limits are not validated here.

items.name: pub fn collect_statistics(arrays: &[&ArrayRef]) -> StatisticsRow {
items.annotation: collect_statistics is pub within the private module and panics with No arrays to collect statistics from on an empty outer slice. It dispatches Boolean, eight integers, Float32/64, temporal families, Decimal128, both binary/string offset widths, FixedSizeBinary and Dictionary based only on the first DataType. Null, Float16, Decimal256, views, structs, lists and other unsupported types reach unreachable; Decimal256 TODO and commented list arms are not support. Returns a row, not Result, and performs no common-type/parameter preflight.

items.name: pub fn supports_stats_collection(datatype: &DataType) -> bool {
items.annotation: supports_stats_collection is deliberately narrower than collect_statistics: Boolean, eight integers, Float32/64, Date32/64, Utf8/LargeUtf8, Binary/LargeBinary and Decimal128 only. Excludes Time32/64, Timestamp, Duration, Dictionary and FixedSizeBinary despite reducer support; excludes all other unmatched types. FixedSizeBinary is commented out. Do not infer that a dispatcher arm enables on-disk writer statistics.

items.name: pub struct StatisticsCollector {
items.annotation: StatisticsCollector derives Debug and owns private BTreeMap<i32,(Field,StatisticsBuilder)>. try_new traverses only roots and struct descendants, filters eligible types, clones each Field and creates a builder. BTreeMap keys are original field IDs, so output sorts by numeric ID; duplicate IDs overwrite an earlier entry during collection rather than error. Empty eligible set returns None. get_builder returns a mutable builder or None for absent ID, without allocation or validation.

items.name: impl StatisticsCollector {
items.annotation: StatisticsCollector derives Debug and owns private BTreeMap<i32,(Field,StatisticsBuilder)>. try_new traverses only roots and struct descendants, filters eligible types, clones each Field and creates a builder. BTreeMap keys are original field IDs, so output sorts by numeric ID; duplicate IDs overwrite an earlier entry during collection rather than error. Empty eligible set returns None. get_builder returns a mutable builder or None for absent ID, without allocation or validation.

items.name: fn visit_fields(schema: &Schema) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Field> {
items.annotation: visit_fields creates reversed root stack, pops in schema order, and pushes reversed children ONLY for Struct. It emits the struct node as well as descendants; eligibility later removes structs. Lists, fixed-size lists, dictionaries and other nested types are emitted without descending. This differs from writer fields_in_batches, which emits scalar leaves in reverse root/child traversal order (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:654-692).
